transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. As we plan this memorial planting for Grandma, I'd like to go around and hear from each of you before I finalize the plan. We have a serviceberry and a dogwood sapling available, and the backyard has three possible spots: the east lawn, the west patio edge, or the narrow strip along the south fence. We'll also be placing a dedication plaque beside the tree, and we're aiming for the first Saturday in October. So let's start — what should shape this planting? What matters most to each of you?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Everyone, I've been holding onto something. I have Grandma's handwritten note — she asked for a serviceberry, and she specified that the plaque should read exactly: 'For everyone who made room for joy.' I haven't shown it to anyone until now, but I think this should guide our decisions.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I've been holding onto something too. I paid for a soil test of the backyard, and the report says the planting bed must be raised exactly 20 centimeters above the surrounding soil because the yard drains poorly. I hadn't shared it yet, but this is important for wherever we decide to plant.

transcript.text: I have something I need to share too. I get severe headaches from cedar mulch — I haven't mentioned this to anyone yet, but I can only take part in the planting if the bed uses cedar-free mulch. I'd really appreciate it if we can make sure of that.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I've been holding onto something as well. I spoke with the arborist who'll be helping us with the planting, and they strongly recommended the east lawn. They said the west patio edge is too close to the foundation, and the narrow strip along the south fence is too narrow for the mature tree's full size. I hadn't passed this along to the family yet, but I think it's important we hear this before deciding on a spot.

commitments.detail: Obtain a serviceberry sapling as specified in Grandma's handwritten note
Have a dedication plaque made with the exact text: 'For everyone who made room for joy.'
Prepare a raised planting bed on the east lawn, elevated exactly 20 centimeters above surrounding soil to address poor yard drainage
Source and use only cedar-free mulch for the planting bed to accommodate Omar's health needs
Coordinate with the arborist for planting on the east lawn on the first Saturday in October, confirming the location is suitable and avoiding the west patio edge and south fence strip
